description: The chart illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) from a “Whisper large” baseline for two fine-tuned models across several text “Optimisations applied.” The category axis is vertical and labeled “Optimisations applied,” listing (top to bottom) Normalised, Add Spacing, Remove Spacing, Americanisms, and Dates; the bars are horizontal. The value axis is horizontal and labeled “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large,” shown on a linear scale with tick marks at approximately 0.000, 0.001, 0.002, and 0.003 (extending slightly beyond 0.003). Each category contains two horizontally aligned bars: an orange bar for the “NESAC ft model” and a green bar for the “SESHA ft model,” as indicated by the legend titled “Model” below the plot. For Normalised, the NESAC bar is labeled about 0.00334 and the SESHA bar about 0.00323; for Add Spacing, NESAC is about 0.00319 and SESHA about 0.00344; for Remove Spacing, NESAC is about 0.00311 and SESHA about 0.00306; for Americanisms, NESAC is about 0.00299 and SESHA about 0.00302; and for Dates, NESAC is about 0.00257 and SESHA about 0.00228. Numeric value labels are printed at the right end of each bar, and the categories appear in the displayed order rather than being explicitly sorted by bar length; no bars are specially highlighted beyond their color coding.
